checks.invariant: Before reading a repository-discovered .stilo/state.json, readStateResult must refuse symlinks, non-regular files (FIFO, character device, directory) and files above a byte limit
checks.result: readStateResult (hooks/stilo-state.js:129-146) calls fs.readFileSync(statePath,'utf8') directly. It does no lstat, no O_NOFOLLOW, no isFile() check and has no byte limit. statePath comes from findStateFiles, whose only test is fs.existsSync (line 87/108), and existsSync follows symlinks. A symlink to /dev/zero, or a FIFO, therefore reaches an unbounded or blocking synchronous read. readStateResult is a separate function from readJsonObject (lines 202-209, the checkpoint/cycle reader). Fixing the existing checkpoint candidate does not fix this path. readState (lines 117-127) has the same pattern but no hook calls it.

checks.invariant: Each hook entry point that resolves the project must bound how long the state read can take
checks.result: stilo-prompt.js#main (line 19), stilo-activate.js (line 9) and stilo-subagent.js (line 8) all call resolveProjeto → readStateResult on every user prompt, session start and subagent start. The prompt hook's own 1 s bound in readStdinJson (stilo-runtime.js:77-80) is an unref'd setTimeout, and it cannot fire while main is blocked in synchronous readFileSync. The only effective bound is the external host timeout.

checks.invariant: The host-level bound and the process-kill semantics that contain a runaway hook read
checks.result: All three hooks declare timeout 5 (lines 11, 24, 37). The POSIX command is `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/..."` and the Windows command wraps node in PowerShell. The source does not show whether the host kills the node process, or only its shell parent, on timeout. Peak memory reached within 5 s is also not source-visible.

checks.invariant: Content read through a symlinked state.json must not be disclosed into agent context
checks.result: For a non-JSON target, the error is the fixed string 'JSON inválido ou truncado' (stilo-state.js:144). A read error injects e.message, which names the link path, not the target. For JSON targets that fail validateState, only the fixed validation error strings are injected, plus state.phase via faseInvalida (sanitiza, 120 chars) (stilo-instructions.js:130-133, 176-183, 210-232). A valid state injects project and updated. Disclosure through a symlink is limited to a `phase` field of a foreign JSON file, so it is hardening, not a finding.

checks.invariant: Sibling readers apply equivalent file-type controls
checks.result: hooks/stilo-diagnostics.js#fileCheck (lines 11-27) uses statSync + isFile() and rejects non-files, but no hook wires that module. The wired readStateResult has no equivalent check, so the sibling controls are inconsistent.

candidates.title: Per-prompt state.json read follows a repository-planted symlink to a device or FIFO, with no file-type or size check
candidates.description: A cloned or extracted project can ship `.stilo/state.json` as a symlink to /dev/zero (git stores symlinks and materializes them by default on Linux/macOS) or as a FIFO (via archive extraction). On every UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart and SubagentStart, resolveProjeto → readStateResult synchronously calls fs.readFileSync(statePath,'utf8') on it. For /dev/zero the read never reaches EOF and the buffer keeps growing. For a FIFO it blocks. In both cases the hook runs until the host's 5 s timeout kills it, the Stilo state injection is lost, and each prompt is delayed. For /dev/zero, memory may also spike by multiple GB on the developer's machine. Concurrent SubagentStart hooks multiply that. If timeout kill reaches only the shell parent, an orphaned node could keep allocating until the system runs out of memory. The trigger persists in the repository until the user removes it. This is a sibling of the checkpoint candidate hooks/stilo-state.js:readJsonObject:unbounded-readFileSync-checkpoint-special-file, but it is a different function on the per-prompt path and needs its own fix.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: hooks/stilo-state.js#readStateResult passes a path taken from repository-controlled discovery (findStateFiles, which only checks fs.existsSync and so follows symlinks) straight to fs.readFileSync(statePath,'utf8'). There is no lstat or no-follow open, no isFile() check and no byte cap. Unlike the unwired sibling stilo-diagnostics.js#fileCheck, it never verifies the target is a regular file. The only bound is the external host hook timeout, because the prompt hook's own 1 s timer cannot fire while the synchronous read blocks the event loop.

trace.description: UserPromptSubmit hook resolves the project for the host-supplied cwd on every user prompt (SessionStart stilo-activate.js:9 and SubagentStart stilo-subagent.js:8 do the same with process.cwd()).
fs.existsSync(<dir>/.stilo/state.json) follows symlinks and accepts any existing target type, including devices and FIFOs.
The single discovered path is passed unchanged to readStateResult.
fs.readFileSync(statePath,'utf8') reads synchronously with no type, link or size check, so it is unbounded on /dev/zero and blocking on a FIFO.

evidence.description: Unconditional readFileSync of the discovered path; the catch at 133-138 only handles thrown errors, not non-terminating reads.
Discovery test is existsSync only, which follows symlinks; no lstat in the module.
Prompt hook self-timeout is an unref'd setTimeout that cannot run while main blocks synchronously inside the 'end' handler.
Only bound is host timeout 5 s per hook; the same applies to SessionStart (line 11) and SubagentStart (line 37).
Sibling reader rejects non-regular files with statSync().isFile(); the wired hook path has no equivalent control.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox on this host, so a resolveProjeto call against a /dev/zero symlink or FIFO fixture could not be executed. The Node 24 readFileSync('utf8') behaviour on a character device (readFileUtf8 fast path: growth rate, bad_alloc versus ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG) is unobserved.
Host behaviour at the 5 s hook timeout is not source-visible: whether Claude Code/Codex kill the node process or only the `sh -c` / PowerShell parent, and whether the prompt proceeds.
Peak RSS within the timeout window, and whether concurrent SubagentStart hooks cause system-wide memory pressure, are unobserved.

Materialization of the symlink depends on the git client config (core.symlinks). It defaults to true on Linux/macOS and false on Git for Windows, so the default Windows host is likely not affected by the symlink vector.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated Linux VM or container with networking disabled, an empty environment, the repo mounted read-only, a memory cgroup limit (e.g. 256 MB) and a 6 s wall-clock limit: create fixture dir F with `.stilo/state.json -> /dev/zero`. Run `node -e "require('/ro/stilo-code/hooks/stilo-state.js').resolveProjeto('F')"`, then record whether it is OOM-killed or still running at timeout, and its peak RSS. Repeat with `mkfifo F/.stilo/state.json` and confirm it blocks until the wall limit. Then `git clone` a local bare repo committing that symlink, with default config, and confirm the symlink is materialized.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner check on a Linux or macOS workstation with Claude Code: open a disposable project containing `.stilo/state.json -> /dev/zero`, submit one prompt, and observe in a process monitor whether the hook's node process is terminated at 5 s (no orphan survives its shell parent), its peak RSS, and whether the prompt continues. On Windows, confirm `git config core.symlinks` is false by default, so the symlink is checked out as a plain text file.

hardening: A symlinked state.json pointing at a foreign JSON file discloses at most that file's `phase` value (120 chars via faseInvalida/sanitiza), or project/updated if it is a fully valid state. Read errors expose the link path, not the target. Not a finding, but lstat-and-refuse would remove it.

readState (hooks/stilo-state.js:117-127) shares the unchecked readFileSync pattern; no hook calls it. Apply the same regular-file/no-follow/size-cap helper to it, to readStateResult and to readJsonObject.
The existsSync→readFileSync gap is a TOCTOU in form only: the lower-trust repository author already controls the file content, so the race gives no extra capability.

A large regular state.json is bounded only by V8's maximum string length. Above it, ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG is caught and reported as 'unreadable'; below it, the file is re-read and JSON-parsed on every prompt. A cap of a few KB (state.json is a 6-field object) would remove the per-prompt cost.

Suggested fix: open with fs.openSync(p, fs.constants.O_RDONLY | (fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW||0) | (fs.constants.O_NONBLOCK||0)), fstatSync and require isFile() and size <= 64 KiB, read exactly that many bytes, and report 'unreadable' otherwise. Where O_NOFOLLOW is unavailable (Windows), add lstatSync().isSymbolicLink() rejection. Regression tests: a symlink, a FIFO and an oversize file each yield status 'unreadable' without blocking.

uncovered.surface: Agent writes to .stilo/state.json in response to injected instructions ('Corrija o state.json antes de agir', 'grave você mesmo a fase seguinte em .stilo/state.json')
uncovered.boundary: A repository-planted symlinked state.json resolving outside the project, which the agent's write tool may follow and overwrite (e.g. a user dotfile)
uncovered.reason: The hook never verifies the discovered state.json is a non-symlink regular file inside the project before telling the agent to repair or rewrite it. Whether the host write tool and permission system resolve the symlink target is an agent/host behaviour outside this read-path unit, and no assigned unit covers it.
